description:
No spec subject — repo agent-rules accuracy fix.

.claude/rules/beadwork.md and .claude/rules/specled.md both document the subject-to-ticket lookup as:

    bw list --grep "Advances:.*<subject.id>"

bw list --grep is a LITERAL substring search over title and description (bw list --help: '-g, --grep TEXT  Search title and description'). The '.*' is matched literally, so the documented form returns 'no issues found' for every subject. Verified 2026-07-26 against untouched tickets: 'Advances:.*specled.realized_by' returns nothing, 'Advances: specled.realized_by' correctly returns specled_-l05.

Impact is a silent zero, not an error — an agent following the rule file concludes no tickets advance a subject and proceeds on that false premise. That is the same fail-quiet shape the specled_-233 epic tickets exist to remove.

Fix: correct both rule files to the literal form 'bw list --grep "Advances: <subject.id>"'. Check whether any skill or workflow file in the vault copies the regex form too. Consider whether bw list should gain a real regex mode, or whether --grep should reject a pattern containing regex metacharacters rather than silently matching them literally.

Found by the orchestrator during specled_-233 admission while verifying the Advances: line survived a description rewrite.

Note that both files begin with `<!-- agent-rules: generated v0.13.2 -->` (beadwork.md:1, specled.md:1). Per .claude/scripts/rules-check:19 the `generated` state means "rendered from a central template; safe to re-sync" — a future `agent-rules` sync will overwrite an in-place edit. The durable options are (a) fix the upstream agent-rules template for beadwork/specled at v0.13.3+ and re-sync, or (b) flip the marker to `<!-- agent-rules: ejected v0.13.2 -->` (rules-check:20 "was central, now repo-owned; never re-rendered"). Do (a) if the upstream template is reachable in this PR's scope; otherwise land the edit in-tree and record the drift, because ejecting has the side effect of freezing all future upstream improvements to those two rule files.

Explicitly OUT of scope for this repo: the ticket's closing "consider whether bw list should gain a real regex mode, or whether --grep should reject regex metacharacters" — that is a change to the `bw` binary, which is not in this repository. If it should be tracked, it needs a separate ticket in the beadwork project, not code in specled_ex.

== RISK NOTES ==

Spec requirement ids: NONE touched. This ticket has no `Advances:` subject ("No spec subject — repo agent-rules accuracy fix" per the ticket body). It cannot collide with any other ticket's spec requirement edits.

File conflicts: I checked the titles of all 21 sibling tickets in the set. None targets `.claude/rules/*`. The nearest neighbours are documentation tickets aimed elsewhere — specled_-z5t targets skills/spec-led-bootstrap/references/adoption-phases.md, specled_-4pl targets a .spec/decisions ADR, specled_-yds targets docs content-lint test helpers. No file+region overlap. Safe to land in any order within the single PR.

Ordering: no dependency on any other ticket landing first, and nothing depends on it.

Gates: this change executes no code and is not markdown the formatter touches, so `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, `mix test`, `mix format --check-formatted`, and `mix spec.check` are all unaffected. There is no gate that would catch a regression here — which is precisely why the bug survived since 0.8.0. If the orchestrator wants durable protection, the only in-repo mechanism would be a new docs content-lint assertion, which overlaps conceptually (not textually) with specled_-yds's docs content-lint helper work; coordinate if that ticket adds a rules-file lint surface.

Sync hazard (the one thing an orchestrator must not miss): both files are agent-rules `generated v0.13.2`. An in-place edit is silently reverted by the next `agent-rules` sync, re-opening this exact bug with no signal. Decide eject-vs-upstream before merging, and record the decision in the PR body.
